results.rationale: Both opinions are fully uncertain (u=1) so the base-rate atomicity is the only signal; A's atomicity (0.0067) is ~7x B's (0.0009), indicating stronger accumulated evidentiary weight for the supernova-triggered YD-cooling airburst claim than for the inconclusive Taurid-stream/megafaunal-extinction claim.

With u=1 for both, atomicity is the deciding signal; A's atomicity (0.00247) modestly exceeds B's (0.00150), giving a mild edge to the corroborated Taurid-swarm/YD-onset-cooling reading over the gamma-ray/termination claim, though the margin is not large.

A remains fully uncertain with projected probability equal to its atomicity (~0.00055), while B carries explicit disbelief (d≈0.50), roughly halving its projected support (~0.00028); active disbelief in B (evidence pushing against the megafaunal-extinction/gamma-ray/-12000..-11001 reading) favors A.

Atomicity is identical for both (0.00055) with full uncertainty, so no opinion-based edge; using model-prior chronology, A's -13000..-12001 interval sits closer to the widely-cited ~-10950 YD-onset date used elsewhere in this dataset than B's -20000..-19001 interval, which is far removed from established megafaunal-extinction/YD timing, giving A a slight plausibility edge.
